title: Fyllingen rally from 2-1 down to claim BLNO title in epic five-game final against Gimle
description: Fyllingen BK are the 2025-26 BLNO champions, completing a dramatic comeback from a 1-2 series deficit to edge Gimle 80-76 in a pulsating Game 5 decider and win the best-of-five finals 3-2. The Bergen club, who topped the regular season at 23-4, had to do it the hard way against a Gimle side (22-5) that pushed them to the absolute limit across a five-game series in which all four home teams won before Fyllingen broke serve in the decider. Gimle had taken Game 1, Fyllingen leveled in Game 2, Gimle edged Game 3 to lead 2-1, and Fyllingen forced the decider with a Game 4 victory â€” setting the stage for a winner-take-all showdown.
imageCaption: Fyllingen claim BLNO title in epic five-game final against Gimle (Photo: Fyllingen)

title: Fyllingen defend BLNO title
description: Fyllingen - Kongsberg 67-66 Fyllingen nipped Kongberg in the decisive fifth game of the BLNO Finals to repeat as the champions. Dashawn Davis (188-G, college: MSU) scored 19 points to pace the winners. Kongsberg eked out a 19-16 lead after the first term. The Lions responded with a strong run in the next period to gain 36-33 halftime lead. The Miners regained the advantage in the third term. The visitors snatched a 49-48 lead heading into the fourth quarter. But Fyllingen found the way to bounce back as they stole a narrow victory in the clutch moments and defended their BLNO title. Lars Espe (185-G-1998, college: Barry, agency: BIG) chipped in 9 points for the winners. Marin Mornar (205-PF-1993, college: LMU) and Chris Rollins (198-F-1999, college: UAFS) had 16 points apiece for Kongsberg.
imageCaption: Fyllingen defend BLNO title-Apr 28, 2025

title: Fyllingen celebrate BLNO title
description: Fyllingen - Baerum Basket 104-94 Fyllingen claimed BLNO title. They held off Baerum Basket to complete the sweep of the championship series. The game was mostly controlled by Fyllingen. Baerum Basket managed to win fourth quarter 23-21. But it was not enough to take a lead and get a victory that evening. Fyllingen looked well-organized offensively handing out 22 assists. It was a great evening for American guard Isaac Likekele (196-2000, college: Ohio St.) who led his team to a victory scoring 26 points, 7 rebounds and 7 assists. His fellow American import guard Terrell Brown (185-1998, college: NM State, agency: Worldwide SM) helped adding 26 points, 6 rebounds and 5 assists. The best for the losing side was the former international center Ludvik Bergseng (208-2006) with 26 points and 6 rebounds (on 10-of-12 shooting from the field) and the former international guard Stian Mjoes…
imageCaption: Fyllingen celebrate BLNO title (Photo: basket.no)

title: Gimle defend BLNO title
description: Gimle repeated as BLNO champions. They overcame Froya 104-82 in Game 4 of the championship series tonight to capture the trophy. Milovan Savic (205-C-1987) scored 24 points to pace the winners. Gimle eked out a 21-19 lead after ten minutes. Froya unloaded 30 points in the second term to narrow the gap at one point at halftime 50-49. Gimle however took over in the third term. They triggered a 30-16 run in the period to post a 14-point advantage. Gimle added 24 points in the fourth stanza and raced to the title. Jorgen Odfjell (197-G-2000) finished with 19 points in the win. Ognjen Nisavic (195-G-1992) produced 33 points, while Jurgen Lamo contributed 13 points in the losing case.
imageCaption: Gimle defend BLNO title (Photo: basket.no)

title: Gimle earn BLNO title
description: Baerum Basket - Gimle BBK 74-76 Gimle BBK claimed the BLNO title. They nipped Baerum Basket on the road in Game 4 to lift the trophy. Strangely Baerum Basket outrebounded Gimle BBK 45-31 including 35 on the defensive glass. Worth to mention a great performance of Serbian-Montenegrin center Milovan Savic (205-1987) who helped to win the game recording 19 points and 8 rebounds and the former international guard Mikkel Kolstad (193-1995, college: Nova SE) who added 17 points and 5 rebounds during the contest. At the losing side the former international guard Stian Mjoes (183-1989) responded with 24 points and 6 assists (made all of his eight free throws) and the former international forward Sjur Dyb Berg (201-1996, college: Alaska-Anch.) produced a double-double by scoring 15 points and 15 rebounds. Four Baerum Basket players scored in double figures.
imageCaption: Gimle earn BLNO title (Photo: BLNO)
